name: sleep_wake
note: The daemon is STOPPED mid-scenario, because that is the only way this board ever sleeps. Quiet data is not a quiet host: dispatch() stamps last_host_ms on any host protocol line (proto.c:262) and the daemon answers every 10s ping with a pong (bridge.py:145-149), so a live daemon cannot leave the board 30s silent (HOST_TIMEOUT_MS, proto.c:29) at any poll interval -- an earlier version of this file asked for a 40s gap between steps and would have passed against firmware with sleep deleted. With the daemon gone for 45s the board loses the host, sleeps, and must wake and apply a fresh frame when the daemon returns. The evidence is '[sleep] host back; opening eyes' (ui_sleep.c:100), printed nowhere but inside ui_sleep_run(); the earlier lines of the cycle are printed while nothing holds the port and are lost. The steps replay from the start in the second daemon -- ScriptedProvider stamps its t0 at construction -- which is why min_tx is twice the step count.
